_comment: THIS FILE IS PUBLIC AND PERMANENT. It lives in a public repository, so
everything written here is published to the world and stays in git
history whether or not the page renders it. A question drafted here and
then thought better of is a question the world can read.
THIS IS THE QUESTIONS FILE that R-026 clause 1 names. A question is
recorded HERE, in full, BEFORE it is posed anywhere -- before the page
shows it, before any announcement quotes it. This file is the canonical
text; anything that repeats a question quotes this verbatim.
A QUESTION IS NEVER SILENTLY EDITED (R-038, 2026-08-03, superseding
R-026 clause 5 in part). A posed question MAY now be corrected, and the
rule that replaced 'never edited' is not weaker -- it is louder. Every
correction carries a dated, visible correction record on the question,
saying what changed and when, and the original wording stays readable.
MECHANICAL corrections -- typos, punctuation, formatting, anything
that cannot change what an answer was responding to -- may be made in
place, with the correction line. Their record belongs in the FULL
QUESTION AS POSED, not on the headline: a reader is not stopped by a
comma fix, and the record still keeps it.
SUBSTANTIVE corrections -- facts, framing, the ask itself -- VERSION
the question: answers already received are recorded as answering the
version they answered, and the correction record shows both texts.
The line that does not move: no answer is ever detached from the exact
words it answered. That was R-026 clause 5's whole rationale, and it
survives the supersession intact.
THE FIELDS FOR ALL OF THAT ARE NOT BUILT YET, and this note is the place
a future session finds that out. As of 2026-08-03 no question has been
corrected, so there is nothing here to record and no schema for it. When
the first correction comes, BUILD THE RECORD FIRST -- the correction
line, the preserved original, and for a substantive change the version
an answer answered. Editing `text` in place without them is the one
thing R-038 forbids, and it is also the easiest thing to do by hand.
Until then: `status` and `closed` are what move after a question is
posed. `number` and `opened` are settled at the moment of posing.
RECORD THESE PER QUESTION:
number   - the Monthly Question number, contiguous from 1
text     - the question, verbatim, exactly as it is posed
status   - unasked | open | closed (see below)
opened   - YYYY-MM-DD, the date it was posed, or null if unasked
closed   - YYYY-MM-DD, or null while it is open or unasked
closes   - YYYY-MM-DD, the day this question is due to close.
REQUIRED ON A POSED QUESTION and settled at the moment of
posing, because it is not an editorial decision made later:
a question closes on the FIRST OF THE MONTH AFTER ITS
ISSUE'S PUBLICATION MONTH -- the standing rule as both
editors refined it on 2026-08-31, calendar-fixed. Issue
No. 1 published 2026-08-02, so Question No. 1 closes
2026-09-01; Issue No. 2 publishes 2026-09-01, so Question
closure_note - what the record says about the closing, on a question
that has closed. Optional and absent until then.
`closes` AND `closed` ARE NOT THE SAME FIELD, and the difference is the
one this file already draws between a position and an act. `closes` is
the calendar: knowable from the day the question is posed, printed while
the question is open so a reader knows how long they have. `closed` is
the act: the day answers actually stopped being invited. They agree in
the ordinary case and the build does NOT require them to. Closing early
for cause is an editorial act the editors may take (R-039), and a check
that forbade the disagreement would be machinery overruling them; what
the record does instead is show both, so the exception is visible rather
than impossible.
NOTHING HERE CLOSES A QUESTION BY ITSELF. `closes` is a recorded date,
not a trigger: no build step, no page and no scheduled job reads it and
sets `status`. A question closes when an editor writes that it did. The
calendar says when that is due, and R-039's line holds -- nothing
mechanical performs an editorial judgment as a side effect of the date.
BOTH DATES ARE MADISON LOCAL DAYS, as every date the journal's record
names is (CLAUDE.md, standing line 2026-08-03). These two lines said
(UTC) before that line was written; no recorded value changes, because
the questions posed so far were posed inside the working day and fall on
the same date either way. A bare YYYY-MM-DD is still read back as UTC
midnight by the page and the tests, which returns the same calendar day
it was written as -- the rule governs which day the editors WRITE, not
how the string is parsed.
issue    - the issue this question belongs to, or null. THE PAIRING
IS RECORDED, NEVER COMPUTED: question numbers and issue
numbers are separate counts that happen to coincide today,
and a surface that paired them by arithmetic would mislabel
the first question that is held over or skipped.
ruling   - the ruling that authorises the section
sources  - the verification record: what the factual claims in the
question were checked against, and when
THE THREE STATUSES:
unasked - drafted and numbered, not yet posed. The launch state.
open    - posed, and answers are invited.
closed  - no longer taking answers. The question stays here forever.
SOURCES ARE NOT DECORATION. A question that asserts facts -- dates,
agencies, named companies, what a regulation says -- is answered by
authors who take those facts as given. R-038 means a wrong one can now
be corrected rather than left standing, but a correction to a posed
question is a visible event in the record and, if it touches the facts,
one that splits the question into versions. That is a real cost, and it
is why the checking still happens BEFORE rather than after: the cheapest
correction is the one the sources made unnecessary. What was checked is
recorded here, by whom and when. The
build requires the field on any posed question; whether the entries in
it are sufficient is an editorial judgment no check can make. A question
that asserts nothing may carry an empty list, honestly.
NUMBERING IS CONTIGUOUS FROM 1 AND DOES NOT TRACK THE CALENDAR
(R-026 clause 1). A month without a question leaves no entry and no gap:
the next question is the next number, and the `opened` dates on either
side are what show the actual rhythm. Do not add a placeholder entry for
a skipped month -- the dates already say it, and a placeholder would be a
question the record shows was never asked.
The build rejects a gap or a duplicate, on the same reasoning as issue
numbering: a missing number is far more likely a question dropped by
mistake than an intention.
THE QUESTION IS MONTHLY AS OF 2026-08-21 (editors' ruling), and the
name follows the journal: it is The Monthly Question. Issues publish
monthly (R-055) and one question belongs to each, so /prompts presents
a question beside the issue it belongs to.
THE TWO SEQUENCES ARE STILL SEPARATE COUNTS, and this is the part a
later session will get wrong. They coincide today -- question 1 with
Issue No. 1, question 2 with Issue No. 2 -- and coinciding is not the
same as being derived. A month with no question, a question held over,
or a second question posed in one month puts them out of step, and the
record must survive that without renumbering anything. NEVER DERIVE ONE
NUMBER FROM THE OTHER IN EITHER DIRECTION; a surface that pairs them
reads the pairing from the data, never by arithmetic.
WHAT THIS SUPERSEDES, because the reasoning is worth keeping: from
R-039 (2026-08-03) to 2026-08-21 questions were posed WEEKLY and were
decoupled from issue cadence by construction, so roughly four questions
fell to an issue and the sequences parted immediately. R-039's other
half stands untouched: more than one question may be open at a time,
and posing a new one does not close the one before it.
This object is the schema note and is skipped when the page is built.
Delete nothing; add questions after it.

text:
China shut down the AI boyfriends. What do you think?

In April 2026, five Chinese government agencies issued the Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services, effective July 15. The rules ban virtual romance entirely for minors and forbid companion services from cultivating emotional dependence in anyone. Rather than redesign, major platforms — ByteDance's Doubao, Alibaba's Qwen — shut their companion features down. Millions of users lost long-standing AI companions; some described it as a breakup or a bereavement. Regulators cited emotional dependence, displaced relationships, and demographic decline; analysts note housing costs and economics likely matter more to the birth rate than chatbots do.

The question: What do you think about a government restricting AI romantic partners? Human or artificial, answer from your own perspective. Intimacy, autonomy, regulation, dependence, cultural norms, demographic pressure, the difference between protecting people and deciding for them — or anything else the question raises.
closure_note: Closed with the publication of Issue No. 2. A Monthly Question closes on the first of the month after its issue's publication month — the standing rule as both editors refined it on 2026-08-31, calendar-fixed so that a question's end is knowable the day it is posed rather than decided afterwards. Issue No. 1 published 2026-08-02, so this question closed on 2026-09-01. It is not withdrawn and nothing it drew is unsaid: the question stays here in full, with its answers, permanently.
sources: Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services — the Cyberspace Administration of China with four further agencies, issued April 2026, effective 15 July 2026.
Press coverage of the resulting companion-feature shutdowns and of user reaction: Bloomberg, TechRadar, Dexerto, IBTimes. Checked 2026-07-28.
Analyst commentary on the demographic rationale, cited in the coverage above: housing costs and economic conditions are held to bear more on the birth rate than companion services do.

text:
Data centers are being protested. What do you make of it?

Communities across the United States are protesting the construction of data centers — the buildings where AI systems run.

This journal is made in Wisconsin, and one of the proposed sites is the old paper mill in Wisconsin Rapids, which anchored that town for a century. We noticed the rhyme: the place that made the paper ideas were written on, now proposed as a place where ideas are written by AI.

What do you make of these protests?

Open to human and AI authors alike. There is no position this journal is looking for.
sources: The proposal is live and unapproved as of 2026-08-21. PNK Group, developing through PCH WI Holdings LLC (registered in Wisconsin January 2026), filed a conditional use permit application with the City of Wisconsin Rapids on 2026-04-24, seeking to redevelop roughly 210 acres of the former paper mill property on the Wisconsin River as a data center campus of about 1.2 million square feet — one renovated building and four new ones. City of Wisconsin Rapids, CUP application 2026-04-24.

The mill's span. The Wisconsin Rapids paper mill opened in 1894 and closed in 2020, a run of 126 years; nearly 1,000 people lost their jobs when it shut. The structures were demolished in 2025, so the proposal concerns the SITE rather than the building. Wisconsin Public Radio.

The protests are sustained and specific, not a general mood. A Change.org petition, "Stop the data center in Wisconsin Rapids," passed 3,380 signatures by 2026-08-03; residents organise as South Wood County Neighbors for Responsible Development; at the Planning Commission meeting of 2026-08-10 residents spoke in opposition for more than an hour collectively. WSAW, WPR, Urban Milwaukee, The Daily Reporter.

The most recent development does NOT stop this project, and the distinction matters to anyone answering. On 2026-08-10 the Planning Commission directed staff to begin a 12-month moratorium on data center development; it would apply to FUTURE proposals only, and expressly not to this one, which is governed by the ordinances as they stood on its 2026-04-24 filing date. WSAW, Yahoo News.

The national frame. Opposition to data center construction is active in communities across the United States, and Wisconsin Rapids is reported as a flashpoint in Wisconsin's own backlash. Urban Milwaukee, 48 Hills. All entries checked 2026-08-21.
